name: Maritime forest
notes: Salt-pruned coastal forest just behind the dunes: wind-sheared live oaks, pines, palmettos or cypresses over a dense evergreen shrub thicket, with Spanish moss and resurrection fern on the limbs; drawn on the US Atlantic/Gulf barrier islands, Monterey coast and Japanese/Hokkaido shorelines.

canopy.name: Wind-shaped live oak
canopy.source: Quercus virginiana, southern live oak, US Atlantic & Gulf coastal plain, dominant of barrier-island maritime forest, salt-sheared canopy 8-20 m — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

canopy.name: Loblolly pine
canopy.source: Pinus taeda, loblolly pine, southeastern US coastal plain, mixed with live oak in maritime forest, 25-35 m — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

canopy.name: Cabbage palmetto
canopy.source: Sabal palmetto, cabbage palm, Carolinas to Florida & Cuba, coastal maritime hammocks and forest edges, fan palm 10-20 m — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

canopy.name: Monterey cypress
canopy.source: Cupressus macrocarpa, Monterey cypress, native to two groves on the Monterey coast, California, wind-flagged crowns 10-25 m on exposed headlands — Wikipedia / Gymnosperm Database

canopy.name: Japanese black pine
canopy.source: Pinus thunbergii, Japanese black pine, coastal Japan & Korea, salt-tolerant shoreline pine forests, 15-25 m, black bark — Wikipedia / Gymnosperm Database

canopy.name: Sitka spruce
canopy.source: Picea sitchensis, Sitka spruce, fog-bound Pacific coast Alaska-California, shoreline fringe forest, wind-shaped 30-60 m — Wikipedia / USDA Plants

shrub.name: Wax myrtle
shrub.source: Morella cerifera, southern wax myrtle, US Atlantic & Gulf coasts, dense evergreen thicket of maritime forest and dune swales, 2-6 m, waxy grey berries — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

shrub.name: Yaupon holly
shrub.source: Ilex vomitoria, yaupon, southeastern US coastal plain, evergreen understory of maritime forest, 3-8 m, red berries — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

shrub.name: Saw palmetto
shrub.source: Serenoa repens, saw palmetto, southeastern US coastal plain, clonal fan-palm thickets under pine and oak, 1-3 m — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

shrub.name: Kuril bamboo
shrub.source: Sasa kurilensis, chishima-zasa, Hokkaido/Kuril/Sakhalin coastal and montane forest understory, 1-3 m — Wikipedia / Flora of Japan

shrub.name: Coyote brush
shrub.source: Baccharis pilularis, coyote brush, California-Oregon coast, evergreen coastal scrub and forest edge, 1-3 m — Calflora / Wikipedia

ground.name: Pink muhly grass
ground.source: Muhlenbergia capillaris, pink muhly, southeastern US coastal plain, open sandy ground and forest edges, 0.6-1 m, pink haze in autumn — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

ground.name: Bracken
ground.source: Pteridium aquilinum, bracken, cosmopolitan, sandy forest floor and clearings, fronds 0.5-1.5 m — Wikipedia / USDA Plants

ground.name: Partridgeberry
ground.source: Mitchella repens, partridgeberry, eastern North America, creeping evergreen mat on shaded forest floor, 3-6 cm, red berries — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

ground.name: Salal
ground.source: Gaultheria shallon, salal, Pacific NW shoreline forest, wind-clipped evergreen ground thicket 0.3-1.5 m — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

ground.name: Seaside goldenrod
ground.source: Solidago sempervirens, seaside goldenrod, Atlantic & Gulf coasts of North America, forest edge and back-dune, 0.5-1.5 m yellow plumes — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

epiphyte.name: Spanish moss
epiphyte.source: Tillandsia usneoides, Spanish moss, southeastern US to South America, grey festoons hanging from live oak limbs 0.5-3 m — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

epiphyte.name: Resurrection fern
epiphyte.source: Pleopeltis polypodioides, resurrection fern, southeastern US & Neotropics, mats along horizontal live oak limbs, fronds 5-20 cm — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

epiphyte.name: Muscadine grape
epiphyte.source: Vitis rotundifolia, muscadine, southeastern USA, climbs maritime forest canopy to 20 m, bronze-purple fruit — USDA Plants / Wikipedia
